THIS RUN ADDS THE ONE THING ITS PREDECESSORS COULD NOT SHOW: the skip-unchanged path FIRED LIVE. Austin Opera's door returned a full 200 whose body was byte-identical to the last read — the run's own line reads 'stage=fetch decision=not_modified detail=body fingerprint unchanged (10e0129ac332...) — extraction skipped, nothing new to read' — so that source cost one conditional GET and ZERO model calls. Read the counters precisely, because they are not interchangeable: 'fetched': 2, 'extract_calls': 1, 'skipped_unchanged': 1, and 'not_modified': 0. The zero is not a contradiction — it is the honest distinction. The saving came from the BODY FINGERPRINT, not from an HTTP 304: the server sent the bytes and the fingerprint refused to pay a model call to read them again. The 304 half of the same Must-do therefore still rests on hermetic and real-Postgres coverage only, not on this run. Paramount Theatre (Austin) is the other half of the pair and the control: its page HAD changed, so it was the one page sent to the model, producing 24 candidates and a gate PASS awaiting authenticated ops promote. Both sources ran from the REFRESH queue at ONE fetch each ('the known best door answered, so no probe was spent') — neither homepage was re-discovered, which is the point of the door. MEASURED SPEND, reported by the run itself: 1 extract call, 10,732 input / 1,796 output tokens read back from the provider's own _usage stamps, priced at $0.0986 from the committed ladder in docs/MODEL_ROUTING.md. SCOPE LIMIT: this run exercised the REFRESH queue only — both sources already had a best_url and the planner reported 0 event-proximity pages due — so it certifies that the runtime RUNS, that refresh works live, and that the fingerprint skip works live, and claims nothing about the DISCOVER probe path or the EVENT-proximity ladder beyond their hermetic and real-Postgres coverage (tests/test_fair_crawl.py, tests/integration/test_crawl_state_pg.py).
